query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for jet-turbine applications, what single intervention could improve high-temperature mechanical capability while limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its mechanism, the expected improvement relative to a relevant baseline, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive experiment with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding 15 vol% Al2O3 nanoparticles to a TaNbVTi-based RHEA will induce in-situ formation of fine TiO precipitates that strengthen the alloy at high temperatures via dispersion and precipitation strengthening, while reducing overall density and preserving room‐temperature ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: TaNbVTi-based refractory high-entropy alloy produced by powder metallurgy without any oxide dispersoids.
generation.intervention: Introduce 15 vol% Al2O3 nanoparticles during the ball-milling step prior to spark plasma sintering.
generation.conditions: Mechanical tests under high-temperature (approximately 800–1000°C) compressive or creep conditions relevant to jet-turbine operation, along with routine room-temperature ductility measurements.
generation.structural_mediator: Uniformly distributed, in-situ formed fine TiO precipitates within the ductile refractory matrix.
generation.mechanism: The added Al2O3 acts as ceramic nucleation sites during sintering, promoting the controlled formation of TiO precipitates. These precipitates hinder dislocation motion and stabilize the grain structure at elevated temperatures (improving high-temperature strength and creep resistance), while the matrix remains sufficiently ductile at room temperature and the overall density is reduced via the lightweight oxide addition.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to a baseline TaNbVTi alloy without Al2O3, the modified alloy is anticipated to exhibit an approximate 30% enhancement in high-temperature yield strength/creep resistance, a 15% reduction in density, and comparable room-temperature ductility.
generation.baseline: TaNbVTi refractory HEA processed identically but without the addition of Al2O3.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to TaNbVTi-based alloys processed via powder metallurgy and SPS; the effects may differ if processing conditions or compositions are significantly altered, or if tested under conditions far outside the 800–1000°C range.
generation.uncertainty: While experimental evidence supports room-temperature improvements and density reduction due to oxide additions, the precise magnitude of high-temperature mechanical improvements and long-term stability under cyclic/creep conditions have inherent uncertainty.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of TaNbVTi-based samples: one baseline alloy without Al2O3 and one with 15 vol% Al2O3 using identical ball-milling and SPS parameters. Conduct high-temperature compressive tests (e.g., at 800–1000°C) and creep tests, along with room-temperature tensile/ductility measurements, and density measurements.
measurements: High-temperature yield strength (or creep resistance) at ~800–1000°C
Microstructural characterization (to verify formation and distribution of TiO precipitates)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 15 vol% Al2O3 alloy does not show at least an approximate 30% improvement in high-temperature mechanical performance relative to the baseline, or if room-temperature ductility is significantly compromised (e.g., degraded by more than 20%), then the hypothesis will be falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractA series of novel lightweight TaNbVTi-based refractory high entropy alloys (RHEA) were fabricated through ball-milling and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The reinforced phase of TiO precipitates were in-situ formed due to the introduction of Al2O3 ceramic particles. The RHEA with 15% Al2O3 exhibits a high compressive yield strength (1837 MPa) and a low density (7.75 g/cm3) with an adequate ductility retention. The yield strength and density are 32% higher and 15% lower, respectively, compared to the RHEA without Al2O3 addition. The specific yield strength (237 MPa cm3/g) of the RHEAs is much higher than that of other reported RHEAs, and is mainly ascribed to the introduction of high volume fraction of Al2O3 additives, resulting in solid solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening. Meanwhile, the ductile matrix is responsible for the good compressive plasticity.Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, powder metallurgy, sintering, mechanical property

Nevertheless, the specific strength of this alloy is only 151.48 MPa∙cm3/g, which has the potential for further improvement. In this work, a series of lightweight TaNbVTi-based RHEAs were fabricated by mechanical alloying (MA) followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS). The microstructural evolution and its effects on mechanical properties were analyzed.
## 2. Experimental Procedures
The TaNbVTi-based RHEAs were prepared by powder metallurgy (P/M) method. High purity (>99.5 wt.%) Ta, Nb, V, Ti elemental powders in equiatomic composition were mixed with Al2O3 powders as the raw materials, and then blended with a planetary ball-millers for 6 h at 120 rpm under argon atmosphere at a temperature of 25 °C. The average particle size of Ta, Nb, V, Ti and Al2O3 powders is 24.5 μm, 26.1 μm, 22.6 μm, 29.1 μm and 0.3 μm, respectively.
